instruction: I need to prepare this spreadsheet for a presentation. Could you resize the cells to ensure everything fits on a single page when exported to PDF? Keep the PDF name the same as the spreadsheet and save it under /home/user/.

metadata.explanation: Presentation-focused task variation. Evaluator verifies single-page PDF output with proper content.
metadata.verification_details: Uses existing check_pdf_pages metric to verify: (1) PDF file exists at /home/user/Resize_Cells_Fit_Page.pdf, (2) PDF has exactly 1 page (relation=eq, ref_value=1), (3) PDF file size > 10KB (verify_content=True). No custom functions needed as check_pdf_pages is already available in desktop_env.evaluators.metrics.pdf.

llm_judge_reasons: Semantic mismatch in content verification: The task involves exporting a LibreOffice Calc spreadsheet to PDF, which typically produces text/vector-based PDF content, not rasterized images

The verify_content=true flag in check_pdf_pages (pdf.py:39-58) specifically checks for embedded images in the PDF, which will likely fail for spreadsheet exports that contain cell data as text/vector graphics

The evaluator correctly verifies: (1) PDF exists at correct location, (2) PDF has exactly 1 page, (3) file size > 10KB, but the image verification logic is semantically inappropriate for spreadsheet-to-PDF conversion
At runtime, the image check (lines 46-58) will likely return 0.0 even when the task is completed correctly, causing false negatives
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Remove the verify_content flag or set it to false, since file existence, page count, and file size checks are sufficient for this task

If content verification is needed, modify check_pdf_pages to have different content verification strategies based on source document type (spreadsheet vs image), or create a spreadsheet-specific verification that checks for text content instead of images
Alternative: Keep only file existence, page count (eq 1), and file size checks, which adequately verify that the spreadsheet was successfully resized and exported to a single-page PDF

rule_validation_issues.msg: metric check_pdf_pages first parameter type (str) may not match getter get_vm_file return type (Union)
